description: How the model check takes a location ns:path, as Minecraft's ResourceLocation.tryParse does: input.location -> {valid, namespace, path} — valid: the path (all after the first colon, or all) holds only a-z 0-9 / . _ - and may be empty, the namespace (before the colon) only a-z 0-9 . _ -; namespace and path as pack.ModelCheck.namespace and path split it, the namespace minecraft when empty or absent. And declarations whose locations are so: input namespace (the declaring file's, for unqualified paths), declaration (the wagon model's JSON), files (ns:path -> text), present (locations that are there, contents unread); a file is named as Minecraft names it (:a and a are minecraft:a); expected: the findings in the check's order (pack.ModelCheck.findings), each {severity: error | warning, finding}: code (ModelFinding.Code.key), subject and index null, params in the line's order, text.

cases.note: a namespace and a path
no colon: all of it is the path, in minecraft
an empty namespace is minecraft too
the path may be empty: Minecraft takes t: (no file has that name)
a colon alone: minecraft's empty path
nothing at all: minecraft's empty path
only the first colon parts: a colon in the path is refused
a capital in the namespace is refused
a capital in the path is refused
a space is refused, in the namespace or the path
a slash belongs to paths only
dots, dashes and underscores everywhere
Minecraft reads the characters only: .. and // are a path
letters beyond a-z are refused
a backslash is no separator
an OBJ at :car/car.obj is minecraft's; so are its library and its textures, named so

files.minecraft:car/car.obj:
mtllib car.mtl
v 0 0 0
v 1 0 0
v 1 1 0
v 0 1 0
vt 0 0
o BODY
usemtl body
f 1/1 2/1 3/1 4/1
